field_note: The field is genuinely strong on spines and NSigma fit, the BBL/CCN/USDOT infrastructure-reuse thesis holds, and the NYC cluster plus the two CMS plays are real workflows with owners and deadlines. But the scoring shows one systematic bias: lead magnet strength was assigned without checking whether the regulator or a free tool already hands the buyer the same artifact, and that error repeats across HHVBP (CMS mails agencies their IPRs), PBJ (CMS previews plus SimplePBJ), NPDES (ECHO effluent charts), LL97 (six free calculators including the city's own), and the NYC lookups (dobguard, Violation Watch). A second bias is calendar blindness: buyer urgency was scored off statutory cycles rather than distance from today, inflating the MA crosswalk and IEEPA plays whose pain windows are months away or mostly consumed. Third, the forced-spread rule was ignored; almost nothing in the top 20 sits at or below 4 on any dimension, which is exactly the 7-to-8 mush the calibration doc warns against. Net: one kill (IEEPA, a closing one-time event on a competitor-owned spine with customs-broker licensure exposure), nine demotions with named reasons, and one promotion (elevator CAT1) whose honest mid scores now beat the deflated candidates ranked above it.
